title: fix(auth)!: an unmapped SAML sign-in reads the standard email and name claims before the NameID; SSO creates accounts only for email addresses
body:
Fixes #32146

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — narrowed: a new account a SAML or OIDC sign-in would create through an `@better-auth/sso` provider is refused `403 INVALID_EMAIL` (`error=INVALID_EMAIL` on the sign-in's error redirect) when the email the sign-in resolved to is not an email address, with SSO domain verification off as well as on. Widened: for each SAML attribute-mapping member a provider leaves unset, the sign-in first reads the standard claim the assertion carries (`.../identity/claims/emailaddress`, `givenname`, `surname`, `name`). No first-party composition in this repository registers a SAML or OIDC provider.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no skill under `skills/**` teaches the SAML attribute mapping or SSO account creation; `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` gains both rules in this change.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:SAML 登录在管理员没配属性映射时,先读 Entra ID / AD FS 默认发送的标准声明(emailaddress、givenname、surname、name),再退回 `email` 属性与 NameID;另外,无论是否开启域名验证,SSO 只为真实邮箱地址建账号,否则以 `INVALID_EMAIL` 拒绝。
- **为什么改**:Entra 不发 `email` 属性,未配映射时账号邮箱取自 NameID:从登录页进入是 UPN,从 Entra「我的应用」进入是不透明的持久 ID,同一个人会多出第二个账号(而且带着映射的权限集)。
- **风险与回滚**:SAML 或 OIDC 提供方若把用户解析成非邮箱值(只发不透明 NameID、或映射到用户名声明),新用户将不再被创建(已有账号不受影响);回滚即 revert 本 PR。读取标准声明依赖供应商内部行为(见 Acceptance notes),供应商升级若改变它,端到端测试会变红。
- **先看**:`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-saml-standard-claims.ts`(整个机制与其对供应商的依赖)· `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts` 末尾的 `refuseSsoAccountWithoutAddress` · `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` 中 `runSsoCallback` 的 SAML 分支。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/sso-saml-refusal-landing.test.ts -t "standard claims"`,预期 10 个用例全绿;其中「SP-initiated then IdP-initiated」与「portal-first」两例显示两次进入后只有一个账号,第二次进入被拒(account_not_linked)。
- **需要你做的**:决定同一人从 IdP 门户第二次进入时,是否应自动登录到同一账号(今天按平台关联规则以 `account_not_linked` 拒绝,不再建第二个账号)—— 选项见报告的 needs_user_decision。

## What changes

- **An unmapped SAML sign-in reads the standard claims before the NameID** (`sso-saml-standard-claims.ts`). For each of `email`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `name` the provider's mapping leaves unset, a sign-in whose assertion carries the standard claim (`http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress`, `givenname`, `surname`, `name`) reads it before the vendor's own default and before the NameID. A mapped member is read as mapped; a provider that sends `email` and none of these claims signs in exactly as before; when the mapping is unset and the assertion carries both a plain `email` attribute and the `emailaddress` claim, the standard claim takes precedence (where the two differ, a new account is created at the claim address; an existing account still signs in by its account key). The stored mapping is never written.
  - Mechanism: `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 reads one attribute name per member off `samlConfig.mapping` and offers no seam between verifying the assertion and resolving the user. So the ACS request's posted response is read once, before the vendor runs, for the attribute NAMES of its one unencrypted assertion (values always come from the vendor's verified extract), and the adapter's read of that provider's row in that request hands the vendor a mapping that also names those claims, as non-enumerable members so the vendor's provider fingerprint (taken at the sign-in's start and again at the ACS) does not change.
- **Verification on or off, an SSO provider creates an account only for an email address** (`refuseSsoAccountWithoutAddress`, wired into `validateUserInfo` after the proven-domain rule). A SAML or OIDC creation whose resolved email is not an address is refused `INVALID_EMAIL` (an existing ledger code for plugin-auth) with a description naming the remedy and not the value. With verification on, the proven-domain rule still answers first (`EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`), unchanged. Existing accounts, linking and non-SSO creations are unchanged.
- Docs: `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` (the register table, the mapping section, the verification section). Changeset: `patch`, declared BREAKING with its ADR-0087 disposition.

## Tests

All end-to-end cases run the real `AuthManager` with the real `better-auth` + `@better-auth/sso` over the in-memory engine; the IdP is played with the vendor's own `samlify`, signing with a key generated in the test (`sso-saml-refusal-landing.test.ts`, two new top-level `describe` blocks in the existing harness):

- SP-initiated (email-format NameID = UPN) then IdP-initiated (persistent opaque NameID), Entra default claims: one account `mia.chen@acme.com (Mia Chen)`; the second entry reaches it and is refused `account_not_linked` by the platform's linking rule, verification off and on. IdP-initiated first: the account is made for the address, never the opaque id.
- Claim before an `email` attribute; the `name` claim when no given/surname; an admin-named member wins; a stored mapping naming only the groups attribute still completes an SP-initiated sign-in (fingerprint); CONTROL: an `email`-only IdP is unchanged; CONTROL: the stored mapping is unchanged.
- No email attribute/claim and an opaque NameID: refused `INVALID_EMAIL`, nothing written (IdP- and SP-initiated); CONTROL: an address is admitted.
- Pure halves: `sso-saml-standard-claims.test.ts` (name reading: encrypted, two or nested assertions, oversize, non-XML read nothing; member choice; the adapter read half incl. non-enumerability and no mutation of the engine object), and a new `describe` in `sso-account-at-proven-domain.test.ts` (SAML and OIDC, refusal names no value, only SSO creations judged).

Ablations (each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on a committed head, restore verified as blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty):

1. Drop the adapter read half (`applyStandardSamlClaimsOnRead` in `findOne`): 8 of the 9 standard-claim cases red; the `email`-only CONTROL stays green.
2. Make the added mapping members enumerable: exactly the 3 SP-initiated cases red with `error=invalid_state&error_description=sso_provider_changed_during_authentication` (the fingerprint).
3. Unwire `refuseSsoAccountWithoutAddress`: both `INVALID_EMAIL` cases red; the CONTROL stays green.

## Acceptance notes

- **Vendor reliance.** The standard-claim read depends on `@better-auth/sso` reading `parsedSamlConfig.mapping` off the object the adapter returns, and fingerprinting only enumerable members. A vendor upgrade that copies the config first returns the old defaults (ablation 1 shape: the end-to-end pins go red); one that fingerprints non-enumerable members refuses SP-initiated sign-ins at the ACS (ablation 2 shape). The durable fix is upstream: a default-candidates option for the SAML mapping.
- **Encrypted assertions** carry no readable names before the vendor decrypts them, so such a provider reads only what it maps (documented).
- **The second, IdP-initiated entry is refused `account_not_linked`, not signed in**: the account the first entry made is not email-verified, and an unverified provider is not trusted to link itself to an existing account. Whether that entry should sign in to the same account (key on a stable attribute, or a verified link) is a product choice, reported to the dispatching seat, not decided here.
- **Form text, not changed here**: `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts` (held by another card) still says the SAML email member "Defaults to "email", then the NameID", and the mapping summary says "Empty means the default: email from "email" (SAML: then the NameID)". Both now read the standard claim first; the help text wants that sentence.
- **Console copy**: `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/ssoCallbackRefusal.ts` maps no sentence for `INVALID_EMAIL` (nor, already, for `EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`) on an SSO callback, so the end user reads the generic "the sign-in link expired or was already used" with the code behind the details toggle. Read from the code, not measured in a browser.
- An Entra user whose `mail` differs from the UPN and who already has an account keyed on the UPN (made before this change) still has that account found by its account key on SP-initiated sign-in; an IdP-initiated entry now resolves to `mail`, finds no user by that address, and creates one (as an opaque-id account was created before).

Taken before the merge with `origin/main` at `946912a7a`; the merge touched `auth-manager.ts` outside these hunks, and the post-merge suite above compiles every file.
